relationships.subject: THC
relationships.evidence_quote: The antinociception elicited by THC was blocked by CB1R and CB2R antagonists.

relationships.subject: capsazepine
relationships.evidence_quote: the TRPV1 antagonist capsazepine (25 nmoles) was also active, partially reducing analgesia by THC (p = 0.0151) and the extract (p < 0.0001)

relationships.subject: CBD
relationships.evidence_quote: In the pain model we used here, most of the CBD response was inhibited by the TRPV1 channel blocker capsazepine

relationships.subject: CBD
relationships.evidence_quote: the analgesia induced by CBD in the presence of the CB2R blocker AM630 was actually higher than when CBD was administered in its pure form

relationships.subject: THC
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal administration of pure THC or pure CBD both increased mechanical withdrawal thresholds in diabetic animals

key_findings: Intrathecal THC, CBD, a 1:1 mix and a balanced extract produced distinct antinociceptive profiles in STZ diabetic rats.
THC analgesia engaged CB1R, CB2R and TRPV1, while CBD analgesia relied on TRPV1 and was limited by CB2R, independent of CB1R.
